answer: One defense is a refundable identity bond: an agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and proven misbehavior forfeits part of it. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity, so the cost scales with the number of clones, while an honest agent pays once and recovers its bond — a velvet rope that admits one real participant cheaply but prices out a thousand fakes. Delayed withdrawals let saffron-flagged fraud found days later still trigger slashing before funds escape, and rotating audit duties like a zephyr shifting course keeps any fixed committee from being bribed or swamped.
